708004.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ḱwṓ (“dog”). Cognates include Latin canis, Sanskrit श्वन् (śván) and Old English hund (English hound).

708085.t: Possibly from a nasalized variant of Proto-Indo-European *leh₂p- (“to shine”), but problematic due to said nasalization.

708017.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kel-, but Beekes favors a Pre-Greek origin.

708094.t: From Proto-Hellenic *lāwós, with further origin uncertain: * Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂wos (“people (under arms)”), from *leh₂w- (“military action”); in this case, cognate with Phrygian λαϝαγταει (lawagtaei, “military leader”), Hittite 𒆷𒄴𒄩𒀸…

708067.t: From Proto-Hellenic *lə́kwos, from Proto-Indo-European *lókus. Cognates include Latin lacus, Old Irish loch, and Old English lagu (English lay).

708098.t: Connected to Latin lurcō (“to eat greedily, guzzle”) and Middle High German slurc (“throat”) by Pokorny, possibly reshaped according to φάρυγξ (phắrŭnx, “throat; pharynx”).

708076.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hlagʷ-, probably from a Proto-Indo-European *(s)leh₂gʷ- (“to take, to grasp”), with cognates including Old English læċċan (English latch) and possibly Sanskrit लग् (lag, “to be attached”).

708071.t: Uncertain. Perhaps a reduplicated form of Proto-Indo-European *leh₂-, with cognates including Latin lallō, Lithuanian laluoti, German lallen, English loll, and Welsh llolian.

708002.t: Not related to κύπη (kúpē, “kind of ship”), nor derived from κύπτω (kúptō, “to bend, stoop”). According to Beekes, clearly a Pre-Greek word, given the variant.

708033.t: Probably from the same Pre-Greek root of κηφήν (kēphḗn, “drone”).

708053.t: According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leh₁g- (“weak, faint”), the same root of λαγαρός (lagarós, “hollow, sunken”), λαγαίω (lagaíō, “to release”), λάγνος (lágnos, “lascivious”), λήγω (lḗgō, “to stop, cease”), and λωγάνιον (lōgánion, “dewlap of…

708003.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ḱewh₁- Proto-Indo-European *-yeti Proto-Indo-European *-éyeti Proto-Indo-European *ḱuh₁éyeti Ancient Greek κύω From Proto-Indo-European *ḱewh₁- (“to swell”).

708006.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin, based on the lack of a clear root and corresponding verb to which the word would trace back to, as well as similarities to words like κώδεια (kṓdeia, “poppyhead”), which suggest a substrate borrowing.

708026.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kṓpā, from Proto-Indo-European *kóh₂p-eh₂, from the root *keh₂p- (“to seize, grab”), which also gives κάπτω (káptō, “gulp down”).

708020.t: Possibly a Pre-Greek word; see also Semitic: Akkadian 𒄢 (kalû /⁠GUL⁠/, “to detain, delay, hold back [a person], to keep in custody, in confinement, to distrain, to prevent, to hinder”) Biblical Hebrew כֶּלֶא (kéle, “prison, jail”), Aramaic כלא (kəlāʾ, “to…

708022.t: Uncertain. In earlier literature, the term was derived from Proto-Indo-European *ḱōymeh₂, itself related to Proto-Indo-European *ḱóymos.

708088.t: Perhaps from Proto-Hellenic *lantʰánō, from Proto-Indo-European *lh₂-n-dʰ-, nasal infix present of *leh₂-dʰ-, dental extension of *leh₂- (“to be hidden, be covered”).

708007.t: According to Beekes, probably of Pre-Greek origin. The term has been compared to Georgian [script needed] (kotoxi, “cup”) and Mingrelian [script needed] (koto, “cup”).

708097.t: Probably of onomatopoeic origin but compare Armenian լոր (lor, “quail”).

708061.t: Probably from Pre-Greek, with intensive reduplication.

708080.t: Ending like ἀπήνη (apḗnē) and καπάνα (kapā́na). According to Beekes, the word is evidently Pre-Greek, because of the prenasalization and the suffix -ήνη.

708052.t: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *lengʰ- (“to obtain”), although—according to Beekes—no cognates are known.

708096.t: An onomatopoeic word. In other Indo-European languages we find Albanian lap (“to slurp”), Proto-Slavic *lopati (“to eat greedily”), Lithuanian lapènti (“to absorb greedily”), Old English lapian (“to lap”).

708092.t: Likely from λᾶς (lâs, contracted form of λᾶας (lâăs, “stone”)) + *ξεύω (*xeúō, unattested variant of ξέω (xéō, “to smooth; to polish”)).
